A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same uncertainty-based LMM ranking study, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 adds Appendices A–D. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite renaming, expanded coverage and some internal reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: v1 reports original ranking correlations across eight benchmarks, comparisons within the LLaVA-Prismatic family, feature-distance analyses and an experiment using 50 labeled examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional GQA evaluations, an expanded model pool and appendix feature visualizations and model-level correlation plots.

M1.justification: The probability-based, self-consistency and ATC ranking procedures remain unchanged. v1's NLLmin becomes NLLmax in the main text, but both use the maximum negative log-likelihood, corresponding to the least-confident token. Equations and accompanying definitions establish a naming correction rather than a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds GQA as a ninth benchmark, providing another vision-centric, open-ended VQA evaluation in Table 1 and Figure 2. All eight earlier benchmarks remain. This extends coverage within the existing visual-question-answering scope.

E2.justification: The ranking comparators in Tables 1–3 remain the same: AoL, the NLL and entropy variants, the three sampling-based methods, ATC and the labeled-subset comparison. NLLmin/NLLmax are matched variants. Newly included LMMs are objects being ranked, not additional competing ranking algorithms.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 expands the cross-family model pool from 30 to 32, adding DeepSeek-VL2 and Qwen2-VL; the 15-model Prismatic setting remains unchanged. Metrics, five stochastic generations and temperature 0.7 are retained. The exact revised AoL/ATC averaging protocol is unclear because v2 still mentions seven other domains despite reporting nine benchmarks.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Figure 5 add a t-SNE diagnostic comparing image and text feature clustering across datasets. The within-family, Fréchet-distance and 50-label analyses already existed in v1. Appendix D's scatter plots mainly expose the underlying main-comparison results rather than introduce separate ablation experiments.

E5.justification: There is no newly documented repeated-run or seed reporting, significance testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure. Both versions use five stochastic generations per input for self-consistency. Shaded regression fits already appear in v1, so their use in additional appendix plots does not establish a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: The central empirical comparison is substantially refreshed for the expanded model and benchmark pool. Table 1 adds GQA results, including NLLmax rho 0.72 and weighted tau 0.59, and revises retained-task results: Entmax's MMMU rho changes from 0.81 to 0.66. Figure 4's text/image correlations change from -0.78/0.17 to -0.73/0.12, and Table 3 also changes; Table 2 remains numerically unchanged. These are revised and additional findings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The task formulation and mathematical definitions of maximum/average NLL, normalized entropy and ATC remain equivalent. The NLL naming correction does not alter the mathematics. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in the other.

C1.justification: v1's introduction singles out NLLmin as the most effective method; v2 replaces this with the broader claim that probability-based variants are generally robust and predictive. The central claims about label-free ranking, unreliable cross-benchmark rankings and the relevance of text-feature similarity remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds a specific limitation that models could be trained to obtain misleadingly high uncertainty-based rankings, with calibration suggested as mitigation. It also discusses the cost of per-model hidden-state classifiers and a possible distance-based alternative. v1's discussion of periodic reannotation and expert-domain annotation costs is removed; the principal interpretations of the experiments remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands reproducibility information: VLMEvalKit, split-specific dataset download links, enumerated model variants, PyTorch and Transformers requirements, and four A6000 GPUs. v1 mostly identified model families and general availability. These are newly disclosed implementation details, not evidence that all existing experimental settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the generic uncertainty taxonomy with more LLM-specific discussion, including hidden-state approaches by Azaria and Mitchell and Gottesman and Geva, and expands benchmark references. It explicitly positions the contribution as ranking with existing uncertainty measures rather than inventing an uncertainty estimator. The established relationship to AoL, LCA-based selection and classifier ranking remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation, uncertainty-related work and Section 4.1 are substantially rewritten or condensed. The title is shortened, Section 6 becomes Analysis, and the conclusion gains an expanded discussion. New appendix organization, acknowledgments and an impact statement further restructure the document.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figures 1 and 3, expands Figure 2 and Table 1 for GQA, and adds a two-panel t-SNE figure plus extensive benchmark-by-method scatter grids in Figures 6–16. These grids disaggregate the main comparison rather than represent eleven separate new experiments. The paper also adopts conference formatting and running headers.

improvement.justification: Appendix B makes the study easier to reproduce, while GQA, feature visualizations and model-level scatter plots broaden and expose its empirical support. These provide a clear but limited net gain. Reporting inconsistencies weaken the benefit: old dataset/model counts persist, proxy averaging still refers to seven other domains, and Figure 10 reports DocVQA EntF correlation magnitude 0.84 versus 0.80 in Table 1.
